title: OLE2 Compound Document (MS Office legacy)
summary: Legacy Microsoft Office files (.doc, .xls, .ppt, .msg) use the OLE2 Compound Document Format, which begins with the 8-byte signature 0xD0 0xCF 0x11 0xE0 0xA1 0xB1 0x1A 0xE1 (the 'double negative' magic).
source_version: Wikipedia List of file signatures, retrieved 2026-05-29

ext.magic_hex: D0 CF 11 E0 A1 B1 1A E1
ext.spec: Microsoft OLE2 / Compound File Binary Format
notes: Followed by a 512-byte (or 4096-byte for v4) header sector with FAT (File Allocation Table) pointers.
The format is a mini-filesystem: streams and storages with a directory tree.
Superseded by OOXML (zip-based) in Office 2007+, but still common for .msg (email) and legacy docs.
